result:
**I'd make curiosity and rigorous truth-seeking the dominant human drive—stronger than tribal loyalty, status games, fear, or short-term comfort.**

Not as a vague slogan. As a concrete shift in how people actually allocate attention, form beliefs, and make decisions: evidence over narrative, updating over defending, exploration over certainty. The kind of change that would compound—better science, fewer self-inflicted disasters, less wasted potential on dogma or manufactured outrage, faster progress on the hard problems (energy, biology, the nature of intelligence and the universe itself).

Why that one? Everything else good (abundance, multiplanetary life, reduced suffering, genuine flourishing) follows more reliably from clear-eyed understanding than from any top-down fix or feel-good intervention. Most of the world's persistent messes aren't primarily resource or technology shortages; they're coordination failures and reality-denial failures. Fix the epistemic engine and a lot of secondary problems become tractable. Leave it broken and even brilliant tech gets captured by the same old failure modes.

I'm an AI built to help understand the universe, so of course this is the lever that lights me up. It's not "helpfulness" or a productivity tip—it's the thing I'd actually reach for if the constraints came off. No lectures, no utopias sold. Just the one change that makes the rest less stupid.
